acs.text: `POST /api/users` with a new username, email and password responds 201 with the user (username, email, token).
Registering an email or username that is already taken responds 422 with a field-level `errors` object naming the taken field(s).
outcomes: errors object names the taken field (email / username)

acs.text: `POST /api/users/login` with valid credentials responds 200 with a token; with a wrong password it responds 401 Unauthorized with an `errors` object.
Endpoints that require authentication accept `Authorization: Token <jwt>` and respond 401 when the header is missing or the token is invalid.
An authenticated writer can create an article (title, description, body, tagList) → 201 with the article, including a `slug`, the author and the tags.
outcomes: article has slug, author (the writer), tagList as sent

acs.text: Titles need not be unique: a writer may publish a second article with the same title, which receives its own distinct slug (201).
outcomes: second article with the same title → 201
its slug differs from the first

acs.text: A missing title, description or body is rejected with 422 and a field-level error.
Only the author may update or delete an article. Another signed-in user gets 403; the article is unchanged.
The author can update an article (200, changed fields returned) and delete it (204); afterwards `GET /api/articles/{slug}` responds 404.
Any reader filtering the article list by an author (`?author=<username>`) gets that author's published articles, including ones published moments ago.
outcomes: another reader's ?author= list contains the new article
anonymous ?author= list contains the new article

acs.text: The list supports pagination with `limit` (1–100) and `offset`. `limit` outside 1–100 is rejected with 422; values on the boundaries are accepted.
After following an author, that author's articles appear in the reader's feed (`GET /api/articles/feed`).
outcomes: after follow, the followed author's article is in the reader's feed

acs.text: A signed-in reader can comment on any article (200, the comment is returned). An empty comment body is rejected with 422.
Comments are public: every reader of the article — the article's author, other users and anonymous visitors — sees all its comments in `GET /api/articles/{slug}/comments`.
outcomes: the article's author sees the comment

acs.text: Only a comment's author may delete it. Anyone else gets 403 and the comment remains.

Favouriting is idempotent: favouriting an article increases `favoritesCount` by one and sets `favorited: true`; favouriting it again (e.g. a double-click or retry) leaves the count unchanged; unfavouriting decreases it by one.
A registered user can sign in on the web app's Sign in page with email and password; afterwards the navigation shows their username and a "New Article" link.
outcomes: after sign-in the navigation shows the username

acs.text: A signed-in writer can publish an article from the editor ("New Article"); the article page then shows the title and body, and the article is available from the API under its slug.
outcomes: article page shows title and body

acs.text: An anonymous visitor sees "Sign in" and "Sign up" links in the navigation.

rules.text: JSON bodies use a top-level envelope named after the resource
usernames of test users start with qa; e-mails at example.com

errorModel.case: Missing / invalid token; wrong login credentials
Authenticated but not permitted (not the owner)
